quote: internal static function decryptByteArray(source:ByteArray, key:int) : ByteArray { ... for(var i:int = 3; i < 256; i++) { if(i % 11 == 0) { temp = int(ba[i]); ba[i] = ba[i + 256]; ba[i + 256] = temp; } ba[i] ^= key; } ... }  ·  resourceFileNameArray:Array = ["shs3resource.swf","musicresource.swf","soundresource.swf","imageresource.swf","bgresource.swf"]  =>  keys h=104 u=117 o=111 m=109 g=103
text: The audio is RECOVERED, not encrypted-beyond-reach. The game's own decryptor is in the repo: ResourceManager.decryptByteArray XORs bytes 3..255 with key = resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1) AND swaps ba[i] with ba[i+256] whenever i%11==0. Applying it to all five Mobile_*Resource.bin files yields valid SWFs. 122_Mobile_SoundResource inflates to 29,623 bytes holding 13 DefineSound tags (deflect, die1, die2, die3, slash1, slash2, slash3, punch, hitmetal, fart, goodkoto, sumo, refund) and 113_Mobile_MusicResource inflates to 1,402,677 bytes holding 13 DefineSound music stems (bgm_lose, safepercussion, safekoto, safeambience, bgm_levelup, bgm_gangnam, flutes, dungeonpiano, dungeonpercussion, dungeonflute, dungeonambience, battledrums, battlechants) — all MP3, 11025 Hz, 16-bit, mono. These are byte-exact original assets, not characterisations from a YouTube rip. A plain whole-file XOR fails 68 bytes into the deflate stream, which is why every prior pass concluded 'unopenable'; the i%11 byte-swap is the missing step.
